sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Contract Research Organization (CRO) for Multinational Drug Trials

stage_1.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only as a service-address arrangement: the registered office must be a physical street address in Alberta where process can be served during business hours. A pure mail-forwarding 'virtual' suite without an Alberta-based registered agent or records office does not satisfy ABCA; a licensed registry agent's physical address is routinely accepted. For an ISIC 7490 CRO, a virtual office is acceptable for the registered office so long as the clinical trial sponsor contacts (investigational site addresses) are real and verifiable. Recommended: professional registered-office + registered records office package.
stage_1.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-Moderate, quantified at ≈12% per annum unannounced inspection probability: registry compliance audits for service of process reliability (5%), CRA/GST desk reviews with site visit history for CRO exporters (6%), and FINTRAC-equivalent enhanced due diligence re-visits by bank compliance (2%); Health Canada GCP remote audits are triggered by sponsor CTAs rather than corporate office presence.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, ss. 1(1), 11(1), 12, 15.1, 20-21 (unlimited liability corporations), 101 (registered office), 102 (records), 103 (notice of directors), 107 (first directors), and 124 (procedural mechanics)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta), together with the Initial Registered Office Address and Notice of Directors
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an Alberta ULC; the initial subscription consideration is determined by the directors, and no escrow deposit is prescribed for a service-based CRO
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the Corporation accepts the subscription for 100 common shares by the initial shareholder at a subscription price of CAD 1.00 per share, and such shares shall be issued as fully paid and non-assessable. 2. That the registered office of the Corporation shall be established at the address set out in the Articles, maintained at an Alberta street address, and all minute books, share registers, and accounting records shall be kept at that office. 3. That [Name] is appointed President, [Name] is appointed Secretary, and [Name] is appointed Chief Financial Officer, each to serve at the pleasure of the Board. The officers are jointly and severally authorized to execute all incorporation filings, open banking accounts, and secure all federal, provincial, and municipal licences necessary for the Corporation's clinical trial management business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) – Corporate Registry System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) through an approved Alberta Corporate Registry service provider or the online Corporate Registry System. Submit a predetermined name containing the formulation 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' or 'ULC'. The search results must be valid for 90 days. After approval, the name is reserved, and the NUANS report is bundled with the articles for filing.
required_dossiers: Three proposed corporate names in priority order
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar objects on grounds of similarity or nondistinctiveness, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request or submit a revised name. An appeal may be made to the Court of King's Bench within 30 days after the objection notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Filing of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) – Online or paper filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in accordance with Form 1 of the Alberta Business Corporations Act, containing the corporate name, the statement of unlimited liability for shareholders, the registered office address (a physical address in Alberta), and the class of shares to be authorized. File the articles, together with the Initial Registered Office Address and the Notice of Directors, with the Alberta Corporate Registry and pay the statutory filing fee. The registry issues a Certificate of Incorporation upon completion of the filing.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) with the unlimited liability provision endorsed
Consent of each initial director and officer to act in such capacity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the articles are deficient, the Registrar issues a requisition letter specifying the defect. The applicant may amend and resubmit the articles within 60 calendar days. Failure to cure results in withdrawal; the applicant may then re-file with a fresh application or appeal the decision to the Court of King's Bench.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry – Notice filing; internal corporate governance authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the inaugural board meeting (or use a unanimous resolution). Adopt the First Board Resolution accepting the subscription for common shares, exempting the initial shares from vesting restrictions, and appointing the officers. Issue share certificates to the initial shareholder. Record all minutes and maintain the share register in the registered office. If there is any change to the officers or directors, file the corresponding Notice of Directors with the Alberta Corporate Registry.
required_dossiers: Written consent of the sole director/secretary
Share certificate stub and share subscription agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director refuses to act or a subscription default occurs, the directors may rescind the subscription and issue the shares to another subscriber as provided by the articles. Any failure to file updated notices may be cured by filing a late amended Notice of Directors and, if required, paying a late-filing fee. Internal remedial actions must be reflected in a directors' supplementary resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Canada Revenue Agency Business Number Registration and Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency – Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the Certificate of Incorporation, register with the CRA for a Business Number and open the applicable tax accounts: corporate income tax, GST/HST (if taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000), payroll source deductions, and an import/export account if trial supplies cross the border. For an Alberta ULC, the corporate tax registration also triggers Alberta Corporate Tax obligations under the Alberta Corporate Tax Act if the corporation has a permanent establishment in Alberta.
required_dossiers: Corporate legal name and street address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA queries a registration, the business must respond through My Business Account or the submitting agent within the deadline, providing corrected information. Missing payroll or GST/HST accounts may be retroactively opened, with penalties and interest waived if voluntarily disclosed under the CRA's Voluntary Disclosures Program before an audit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence, OHS, and Fire Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City business licensing department (e.g., City of Calgary / City of Edmonton) and Alberta Occupational Health and Safety
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an application for a general business licence, business address registration, and, if a laboratory is maintained, for a hazardous materials and institutional licence. Arrange a pre-occupancy physical inspection by municipal fire marshals and building safety inspectors, and install any required safety equipment. Obtain a certificate of compliance under the Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Act and register the workplace with the Workers' Compensation Board. Keep a copy of all permits in the corporate records.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or proof of ownership of the business premises
OHS registration form and workplace policy manual
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal authority denies or imposes conditions, the applicant may appeal to the municipal board or attend a variance hearing. For OHS orders, a corrective action plan can be submitted, and for WCB issues, a reconsideration request may be filed within 30 days. All adverse decisions are amenable to judicial review if statutory timelines and remedy procedures are exhausted.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Health Canada – Therapeutic Products Directorate (Drug Establishment Licensing) / Alberta Ministry of Jobs, Economy and Trade; municipal industrial licensing departments
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Drug Establishment Licence (DEL) under Health Canada Food and Drug Regulations, and General Municipal Business Licence

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B Registration (environmental assessment exemption) for office-only CRO; full EPEA approval required if a BSL-2 laboratory is operated
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: discharge to municipal sewer must comply with municipal sewer use bylaws and Alberta's Wastewater and Storm Drainage Regulation (A.R. 119/1993); VOCs: laboratory operations must maintain VOC emissions below point-source thresholds in the Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives and, if solvents are used, meet NPRI reporting limits; biomedical waste: all clinical waste must be segregated, stored, and disposed through a licensed biomedical waste carrier under Alberta's Biomedical Waste Guidelines, with BSL-2 containment if biological agents are handled.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety: completion of a fire safety inspection and certification under the Alberta Fire Code (NFPA 101 life safety compliance), issuance of a building occupancy permit, and compliance with structural load limits; Occupational Health: a valid Workplace Health and Safety Certificate under the Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Act and WCB account registration if the CRO has employees; Emergency: approval of an emergency response and fire evacuation plan by the local fire department.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada; national electronic portal: My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html) and Business Registration Online (BRO); provincial partner for Alberta: Alberta Treasury Board and Finance, with Alberta corporate income tax administered by the CRA through the Tax Administration Agreement and a single federal T2 filing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: incorporate the Unlimited Liability Corporation under the Alberta Business Corporations Act via the Alberta Corporate Registry and obtain the corporate access number. Step 2: obtain the federal 9-digit Business Number (BN) from CRA by filing Form RC1 Request for a Business Number or using CRA Business Registration Online; select Non-Resident Corporation status and open program accounts RP (corporate income tax), RT (GST/HST), and RC (payroll, if applicable). Step 3: register the Alberta provincial corporate income tax account through the same BN; no separate Alberta TIN exists. Step 4: apply for GST/HST registration; registration is mandatory once worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in a calendar quarter or the four preceding calendar quarters, and voluntary registration is available for sub-threshold entities to recover input tax credits; a non-resident applicant may be required by CRA to provide a Canadian address for service and post security under Excise Tax Act s. 289. Step 5: enroll in CRA My Business Account, authorize a tax representative where needed, and file T2 and GST/HST returns electronically.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible, with dual classification: for U.S. federal tax purposes, the Alberta ULC is an eligible entity that may elect under IRC § 7701 (Form 8832 tax classification election) to be treated as a partnership or disregarded entity and is not a per se corporation. For Canadian domestic tax purposes, the default classification is Entity_Level_Taxation: the ULC is a corporation resident in Canada under Income Tax Act s. 250(2)(a), files a T2 return, and is subject to Part I tax on worldwide income; CRA does not recognize the U.S. check-the-box pass-through status for Canadian income tax or GST/HST purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canadian domestic law has no check-the-box election. Relevant elections and regimes: (1) U.S. Form 8832 tax classification election to make the ULC disregarded or partnership-status for U.S. tax, creating a hybrid structure; (2) GST/HST elections: Excise Tax Act s. 156 election for closely related corporations to charge nil consideration on intercorporate supplies, and ETA s. 240(4) GST/HST group registration; (3) hybrid mismatch rules: Income Tax Act ss. 18.2, 18.3 and 18.4 may disallow deductions or deem hybrid dividends where the U.S. shareholder treats the ULC as a disregarded entity, requiring annual review; (4) treaty-based relief election under the Canada-U.S. Tax Convention, subject to the Limitation on Benefits article; (5) Alberta corporate elections under the ABCA, administered through the federal T2 system.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the central monetary authority; no separate exchange-control administration exists. The Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) supervises all federally regulated deposit-taking institutions. Canada abolished its formal exchange-control apparatus in 1952; foreign exchange policy is now administered by the Department of Finance Canada through the Exchange Fund Account.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility of the Canadian dollar (CAD) on both current and capital accounts; Canada has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations since December 1952. No governmental approval, quota, licence, or registration is required for inbound foreign direct investment, shareholder loans, or the repatriation of profits. Dividend distributions by an Alberta ULC to a US parent are subject to Part XIII withholding tax (statutory 25%, treaty-reduced to 5% under the Canada-US Tax Treaty for a corporate shareholder holding at least 10% voting rights), while arm's-length interest on shareholder debt is exempt from withholding under s. 212(1)(b) of the Income Tax Act. The CAD trades on a free float; the Bank of Canada does not target any exchange rate band.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no surrender, forced conversion, or mandatory repatriation timeline on export receipts, including fees earned by a clinical trial CRO from non-resident sponsors. Foreign-currency proceeds may be retained in any currency, held offshore, or converted freely. The only compliance hooks are (i) FINTRAC large electronic-funds-transfer reporting for each wire of C$10,000 or more, (ii) the CBSA cross-border currency declaration for physical cash movements of C$10,000 or more, and (iii) Form T1135 reporting for a Canadian-resident ULC holding specified foreign property in aggregate above C$100,000.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary banking substitute; Medium as an ancillary payment rail. Canadian law reserves deposit-taking to OSFI-regulated chartered banks and provincial credit unions under the Bank Act and provincial trust-and-loan statutes; offshore digital EMI platforms may not lawfully hold the ULC's operating balances or escrowed milestone funds. An offshore EMI may be used only as a settlement aggregator for minor outbound vendor payments, and only if the EMI is registered under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) with the Bank of Canada and clears through a licensed Canadian payment-service provider. All material trial balances must remain at a Tier-1 Canadian bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance is strongly preferred for at least one director or authorized signatory; fully remote opening is permitted but rarely approved for unlimited-liability structures with 100% non-resident ownership. Tier-1 banks require either an in-person visit to a Canadian branch with original identification or a verified live video interview with a Relationship Manager plus credential-grade electronic ID proofing for every non-resident director and ultimate beneficial owner. FINTRAC obligations under the PCMLTFA require independent third-party verification of all directors, officers, and individuals exercising control; enhanced due diligence is standard for the first 12 months.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity created by the US parent's check-the-box disregard election and the unlimited-liability feature of the Alberta ULC.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta Corporate Registry certificate and a current certified corporate search; register of directors and registered shareholders; US Form 8832 and Form 8858 filings of the parent; signed Beneficial Ownership Declaration identifying every individual with 25% or more control; federal and provincial UBO register extracts; audited financial statements and a capitalization schedule for the ULC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound USD settlement wires from non-resident biopharma sponsors lacking a transparent source-of-funds chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Master Clinical Trial Agreement, detailed milestone invoice schedule, Health Canada CTA No-Obligation Letter, Research Ethics Board approvals; sponsor corporate registry excerpt and AML attestation; bank-to-bank reference letter from the sponsor's home institution; source-of-wealth statement for any milestone receipt above C$1 million; full patient-site payment matrix.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payments to trial sites, investigators, and CRO subcontractors in higher-risk jurisdictions, including sanctions-screening mismatches.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Centralized beneficiary pre-vetting log covering OFAC, Global Affairs Canada sanctions, RCMP, FINTRAC, and OSFI lists; restricted-jurisdiction exception memorandum approved by the bank's compliance team; exclusive routing through high-correspondent-bank channels; per-wire documentation showing the ISIC 7490 service description; timely FINTRAC large-value and suspicious-transaction filings where applicable.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder-loan injections are executed by SWIFT MT103 from the US parent to the ULC's Tier-1 Canadian account with an exact beneficiary-name match and remittance advice reading Capital Contribution or Intercompany Loan. Canadian banks require a payment purpose/reason code; equity draws are recorded against share issuance supported by board resolutions, while loans require a written intercompany agreement with arm's-length interest to preserve the s. 212(1)(b) withholding exemption and treaty eligibility. Any electronic transfer of C$10,000 or more is FINTRAC-reportable; capital inflows exceeding C$1 million trigger banker's inquiry and source-of-wealth verification prior to treasury deployment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement is cleared in CAD through Lynx (Bank of Canada RTGS) and in USD or third currencies through SWIFT MT103 via the Canadian bank's US correspondent on Fedwire/CHIPS. Site and subcontractor payments carry a unique end-to-end transaction reference (UETR), pre-validated beneficiary account information, and purpose codes describing CRO management services; no payment may be routed to a sanctioned entity. Imports of investigational medicinal products and trial supplies may be settled by commercial letters of credit under UCP 600 or documentary collection, with presentation of the Health Canada clinical trial authorization, commercial invoice, and transport documents. All CAD EFTs of C$10,000 or more are captured under FINTRAC reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD forward contracts documented under the ISDA 1998 FX Definitions
Vanilla CAD/USD foreign-exchange options (call and put structures)
FX swaps (spot-forward and forward-forward with simultaneous value legs)
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CAD/USD fixed-to-floating) under the ISDA 2002 Master Agreement
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in less liquid third-currency pairs, with mark-to-market treatment under section 775 of the Income Tax Act when applicable

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days after the anniversary of incorporation or the date of the previous annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may result in administrative strike-off of the corporation after notice period, with associated penalties and potential director liability

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory audit for qualifying private companies under Alberta Business Corporations Act unless public interest company or specific size criteria met
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE)

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO confirmation required by government; maintain and update statutory registers for shareholders, directors, and officers upon any changes or transfers

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 100-500 USD per year for registered office and corporate agent in Alberta
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 0 (no mandatory audit required for most private ULCs)
